title: Add GetIndex accessor for concurrent record parsing
description:
## Description

Adds a `GetIndex()` accessor to the concrete reader that returns the schema index previously read (via `ReadIndex`) or set (via `SetIndex`).

This enables a consumer to parse **disjoint record ranges concurrently**: a worker goroutine can be given the schema once (shared, read-only) instead of re-reading the index, then parse its own byte range over an independent reader. Posit Package Manager uses this to decode CRAN/Bioconductor package records in parallel during graph construction.

It is a method on the concrete `*rsfReader`, **not** part of the `Reader` interface, so callers type-assert and existing implementations/mocks are unaffected.

> Stacked on #30 (buffer reuse). Review/merge that first; this branch targets it.

## Testing

- All existing package tests pass (`go test ./...`).
- Exercised by the downstream consumer (PPM): per-worker readers built with `NewReader()` + `SetIndex(reader.GetIndex())` parse record ranges concurrently and produce byte-identical output, verified under `-race` against PPM's reverse-dependency golden checksums and its all-corpus control-parser differential test.

title: Reuse read buffers in rsfReader to cut per-field allocations
description:
## Description

Every `Read*Field` method on `rsfReader` allocated a fresh `[]byte` per call (a 4/8/10/1-byte buffer for size/float/int/bool reads, and a sized buffer for each string). Across a large file this is millions of tiny allocations.

A reader is used by a single goroutine over one file, so this reuses two buffers held on the reader:
- a fixed `scratch [10]byte` array for the numeric/bool reads, and
- a grown-on-demand `strBuf` for variable-length string reads.

`ReadFixedStringField`/`ReadStringField` already return a copied string (`string(bs)`), so reusing the backing buffer between calls is safe — no returned value aliases it.

## Impact

Measured against Posit Package Manager's full CRAN graph load (~121k records), which is the heaviest real-world consumer of the reader:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Allocations | 5.09M | 3.11M (−39%) |
| Bytes allocated | 365 MB | 309 MB |
| Parse wall time | 236 ms | 214 ms (−9%) |

The win applies to every RSF read path. No behavior change.

## Testing

- All existing package tests pass (`go test ./...`).
- Verified behavior-identical against the consumer: PPM's reverse-dependency golden checksums and its parser differential test (over all CRAN + Bioconductor records) are unchanged when built against this branch.

Sourced from github.com/stretchr/testify's releases.

v1.11.1

This release fixes #1785 introduced in v1.11.0 where expected argument values implementing the stringer interface (String() string) with a method which mutates their value, when passed to mock.Mock.On (m.On("Method", <expected>).Return()) or actual argument values passed to mock.Mock.Called may no longer match one another where they previously did match. title: Create dependabot.yml
V2 Index Reading Fixes
description: There were some uncaught issues with reading the V2 index. We were not recording the reader position correctly, but the error wasn't caught by the unit tests. This fixes these issues to get the V2 CRAN manifest working for PPM.

title: Update to Go 1.21
Better Printing and Indexing
description:
* Adds versioning to the RSF index
  * Legacy behavior if `Version1` is used.
  * New information about indexed arrays is stored in the index when `Version2` is used.
* `rsf.Print` method no longer requires passing a type.
* Adds an `rsfprint` binary that can be built to print the contents of a `Version2` RSF file.
* Adds a `Makefile` with a `build` target for the `rsfprint` binary, and adds the build step to CI.

With these changes, we still default to writing the older `Version1` format since it's required by PPM's PyPI support.

My current plan is to continue using the `Version1` format for PyPI so we don't need to generate two PyPI manifests concurrently. We can start using `Version2` for CRAN and Bioconductor from the start, though, to give us the benefits of the better indexing and pretty-printing during development.

title: Add support for printing RSF data
description: For unit tests and debugging, I've often felt it would be nice to have a `Print` method to print out the contents of an RSF file. This adds basic support for printing. It doesn't support printing arrays of arrays, but I think it will support everything we've used RSF for so far.

title: Support Integer Array Indexes
description:
Adds support for indexing an array with an integer. This may end up being useful for CRAN, since we may want to generate some package arrays that are indexed by the package ID for legacy database-to-RSF migrations.

Best reviewed with whitespace off: https://github.com/rstudio/repository-snapshot-format/pull/6/files?diff=split&w=1

title: More complete object tests
description:
Adds a few more object tests and updates a few existing cases with more complex data structures.

This doesn't change the module; it only affects unit tests.

title: Allow specifying advance element for AdvanceToNextElement
Support updating reader position on Seek/Discard
New Field Types and Backwards Compatibility
description:
* Removes some legacy test code.
* Reorganizes some of the code to avoid large files.
* Introduces support for integer and float data types.
* Adds more unit tests for writing simple objects (arrays, strings, etc.).
* Adds the ability to automatically write a struct field index before the first object.
* Adds the ability to read a struct field index from the RSF file.
* Adds the alternate ability to update a reader with a pre-determined struct field index.
* Adds the `Advance` method and its associated interfaces and implementations. These allow you to:
  * Advance to the end of an element.
  * Advance from the start of an element to a known field.
  * Advance from a known field in an element to another known field in the same element.

I would recommend reviewing generally in this order:
* Review the commit that adds int and float support: https://github.com/rstudio/repository-snapshot-format/commit/aeee427cc331fb0a56eca13bcb77a83de6b01167
* Review the new object writing tests: https://github.com/rstudio/repository-snapshot-format/commit/74ad39b29c29127da6c42ee5823cdd9df5f0b639
* Take a look at the new tests for reading an upgraded object from legacy code. This is at https://github.com/rstudio/repository-snapshot-format/blob/5250e04d324fbc284ea764aec1210baa67a8cb7b/writer_upgrade_test.go, and I would get really familiar with how this works before going further.
* Review the rest of the code, skipping what you've already seen.

title: Add rsf Library and README
description: Adds the `rsf` library and a README to get us started.
